Sam (support): FYI customer AcmeApps reported a burst that caused ~10-15% 429s starting ~11:02 UTC. They saw a bunch of failing generation calls and elevated latency. Org id=84321. I grabbed a few request IDs. Anyone oncall?

ops-bot: ALERT: rate-limiter-service: 429 rate_exceeded detected -> org=84321, bucket=default, rps=250, limit=100, timestamp=2026-03-11T11:02:18Z

Maya (eng-sre): I'm on. Looking at logs now. Can you paste sample request ids from the customer?

Sam (support): here are two: req_01GZ2X8JK0Y4, req_01GZ2X9K1LZ7. Also they said they had a sudden traffic spike after a scheduled email campaign.

Arjun (eng-runtime): Pulling limiter metrics. Prom query: `sum(rate(limiter_denied_total[1m])) by (org)` shows spike for org=84321 matching the timeline. Also see a config deploy last night that toggled limiter mode to `global` for a temporary experiment (PR #542).

Maya (eng-sre): That PR rings a bell — intended for cross-org throttling research but should never have gone to prod default. If limiter is in global mode, bursts from one org can exhaust capacity for others.

Ellie (oncall): Can we flip it back to per-org immediately? What's the control surface?

Arjun (eng-runtime): Yes. There's a configmap `limiter-config` in `prod` that has `mode: global` and `global_rps`. Changing to `mode: per_org` should restore isolation. Quick mitigation: increase per-org burst temporarily while we flip mode.

Maya (eng-sre): I'll patch the configmap now. Command:

```
kubectl -n prod patch configmap limiter-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"mode":"per_org","per_org_rps":"200","per_org_burst":"1000"}}'
```

Maya (eng-sre): Applying patch...

deploy-bot: Started rollout of limiter-service (deploy/limiter) to prod (revision 5f3a2 -> 5f3a3)

Arjun (eng-runtime): Also updating the runtime flag on the limiter pods so they pick up the new behavior without a full restart: exec into leader and call admin toggle endpoint: `curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/limiter/mode -d '{"mode":"per_org"}'`

Maya (eng-sre): Done both. Patch applied and admin toggle returned 200.

ops-bot: METRIC: limiter_denied_total for org=84321 dropped from 180->7 in 2 minutes after config change

Sam (support): AcmeApps says errors are dropping and calls are succeeding again. They saw success rates go from 84% -> 99% within ~3m. They've paused the campaign for now.

Ellie (oncall): Nice. We should still run a quick smoke test and watch for regressions. Can someone run renter traffic sim?

Arjun (eng-runtime): Running lightweight sim against org=84321 and a few neighbors. Sim script: `scripts/loadgen --org 84321 --rps 300 --duration 120`

Maya (eng-sre): Results: neighboring orgs unaffected, per-org isolation now working. CPU on limiter pods spiked but within thresholds. 429 rate for org=84321 ~0.6% during the synthetic peak (acceptable).

Sam (support): I'll follow up with AcmeApps and offer a small credit for the outage window. Need the exact window and impacted request ids for reimbursement/ billing reconciliation.

Maya (eng-sre): Root cause summary (preliminary): accidental promotion of experimental `global` limiter mode in last night's deploy (PR #542) which made the default token bucket global. A single org's sudden campaign exhausted the shared bucket and caused cascading 429s.

Arjun (eng-runtime): Immediate fixes we did: 1) re-patched configmap to `per_org` mode; 2) toggled runtime flag via admin endpoint; 3) rolled limiter deploy to pick up safer defaults (per_org_rps=200, per_org_burst=1000).

Maya (eng-sre): Mitigations for next 24h: add a temporary guard on global mode so it cannot be enabled in prod by default (enforce a feature flag that must be true in k8s secret + approval), add an alert when any single org exceeds 200% of their rolling baseline RPS for >30s, and add a rate-limit override endpoint requiring SSO and audit logs for manual adjustments.
